'''Katrina (Kate) Anne Jolliffe''' is an Australian  [[Supramolecular chemistry|supramolecular]] and [[Organic chemistry|organic chemist]] and professor at the [[University of Sydney]].

In 2002 Jolliffe was awarded an ARC fellowship at the University of Sydney. She was made a senior lecturer in 2007, promoted associate professor in 2008 and full professor in 2009. From 2013 to 2016 she was head of the school of chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kate Jolliffe – Women In Supramolecular Chemistry Network|url=https://research.kent.ac.uk/test-women-in-supramolecular-chemistry/person/kate-jolliffe/#about|access-date=2020-06-05|website=research.kent.ac.uk|archive-date=5 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200605210325/https://research.kent.ac.uk/test-women-in-supramolecular-chemistry/person/kate-jolliffe/#about|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Jolliffe is a Fellow of both the [[Royal Society of New South Wales]] and the [[Royal Australian Chemical Institute]]. In 2020 she was elected a Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kate Jolliffe|url=https://www.science.org.au/profile/kate-jolliffe|access-date=2020-06-05|website=www.science.org.au|language=en}}</ref> She has won a number of awards including the Biota Award for Medicinal Chemistry, A. J. Birch, H.G. Smith Memorial medals, and Margaret Sheil Leadership Awards from the Royal Australian Chemical Institute.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Joliffe |first=Kate |title=Professor Kate Jolliffe, The University of Sydney, Faculty of Science |url=https://www.sydney.edu.au/science/about/our-people/academic-staff/kate-jolliffe.html#collapseprofileawards |access-date=2024-07-24 |website= |language=en-gb}}</ref>

== Research interests ==
Jolliffe's research interests include the development of molecules that recognise and sense anions, and the synthesis of natural and novel cyclic peptides.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Staff Profile |url=https://www.sydney.edu.au/science/about/our-people/academic-staff/staff-profile.html |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=The University of Sydney |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Honours and awards ==

* Winner of the 2024 [[Eureka Prizes|Eureka Prize]] for Outstanding Mentor of Researchers<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eureka Prize 2024 Finalists Announced |url=https://www.miragenews.com/eureka-prize-2024-finalists-announced-1286441/ |access-date=2024-08-13 |website=Mirage News |language=en-AU}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Eureka Prizes 2024: Sydney celebrates four wins in science awards |url=https://www.sydney.edu.au/news-opinion/news/2024/09/05/eureka-prizes-2024-sydney-celebrates-four-wins-in-science-awards.html |access-date=2024-09-16 |website=The University of Sydney |language=en-US}}</ref>
